route: /style-board/ (the style board: module process:timeline, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: The process:timeline steps still have no step number or marker: each row is a bold label beside its text over a hairline, so the six steps read as a definitions table, not an ordered sequence (the same at 390 px, where the labels stack over their text with nothing to count them).
findings.reference: Every competitor step module numbers its steps: blue '01–03' numerals on the three-step process, and a number over each title and text above a hairline on the six-step navy timeline (components.md). This site's own process list variant already does this with its 01/02/03 counter.
findings.fix: In ProcessBlock.astro, render the step number (number(index), as the list and photo-cards variants already do) as a .process-step__marker before each .process-timeline__label, in the accent colour; in patterns.css, make room for it in the label column (on phones, beside the label).

findings.issue: Because the fit sizes the heading to its words across the full content width, the section heading 'What to Send for a Free, Accurate Quotation' is set at page-title size (about 64 px, about 2.5× the 26 px heading of m8-steps of the same module) and runs well past the right edge of its own timeline rows and lead, so the module's heading and body don't share a width.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its section headings well below its page titles, one size for each heading level, and keeps each heading inside its module's column.
findings.fix: In the template's heading fit, cap a section h2's fitted size at the h2 step (below the page title's fitted size) and fit it to the module's own measure (the .process-timeline width) instead of the full content width.
